Hi Alice — great speaking with you and Tom. Summary and next steps below.

Quick answers up front:
- Yes, Redwood supports customer-managed keys (we integrate with AWS KMS and GCP KMS).
- HSM-backed keys are supported for Private deployments via bring-your-own-HSM or partner HSM (FIPS 140-2/3 compatible), but that requires a Private deployment and additional configuration.
- All server-to-server traffic is TLS 1.2+; we support mTLS for customer-to-service connections on Private and Dedicated.
- Data at rest is encrypted using keys managed by Redwood by default; with CMK you control envelope keys in KMS. Logs: request metadata is retained by default for 90 days; request/response payload logging for customer requests is disabled by default for accounts that opt into stricter privacy.

Requested next steps:
1) I’ll loop in Neha (SE) and Dev (Security) with a short appendix that outlines the KMS/HSM flow and sample config.
2) If PayWise wants CMK in AWS KMS, we’ll provide a template IAM policy and an ops checklist.
3) For HSM-backed keys or on-prem HSM, we can schedule a technical deep-dive — this is typically part of a Private deployment engagement.

Attaching a short PDF with options and the draft SLA you asked for.

Best,

Hi Alice — following up with a bit more technical detail and an ops checklist. Key points:

1) CMK flow (AWS KMS):
   - Redwood uses envelope encryption. Your CMK in AWS KMS is used to encrypt/decrypt the data encryption key. Redwood stores only the encrypted DEK.
   - We provide an IAM role that allows Redwood services to call kms:Encrypt/kms:Decrypt for the CMK; you can restrict by condition (source VPC, account).

2) HSM / BYO-HSM:
   - For Private deployments we support integrating with customer HSMs (e.g., AWS CloudHSM) or third-party HSM appliances. This requires network configuration and an onboarding checklist (we’ll provide).

3) In-transit: all connections use TLS 1.2+; mTLS is available for Dedicated and Private. We recommend mTLS for any production traffic carrying PII.

4) At-rest & logs: model binaries, caches, and persistent storage are encrypted at rest. By default we retain request metadata for 90 days. Response bodies are only logged if you enable request/response logging — otherwise payloads are redacted/never persisted. We can offer custom retention commitments as part of an enterprise contract.

5) Disabling logging per route: we support per-route logging controls. SEs can configure a route to not persist payloads; metadata (timestamp, model id, token count) is required for billing and telemetry but can be minimized.

Attached: a one-page network/encryption diagram and a sample IAM policy for a CMK role.

If it helps, we can schedule a 30-minute technical deep-dive next week to walk through the checklist and timings (typical lead time for CMK integration: ~1-2 weeks; HSM onboarding: 4-8 weeks depending on network/HSM provider).

Thanks,
